title: LLM runner: embed a lightweight Go LLM client for the ladder's budgeted agent stage — non-streaming completions, per-call budgets (tokens+wall-clock), config-driven model + fallback chain, context-compaction hook
description: the maintainer directive 09-16: lightweight LLM framework, avoid wastefulness — the daemon runs under stress, so STREAMING IS A NON-GOAL (one buffered request/response per stage; a hung stream is the failure mode we refuse). Plain net/http against OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoints (NO heavy SDKs — this is the lightweight framework). Config: [llm] blocks with base_url/api_key-ref/model/max_tokens/timeout per role, plus fallback_chain = ordered endpoint list; a stage tries candidates in order on transport/5xx/429 errors, records which candidate served in the ledger. Budgets: hard caps enforced pre-request (max_tokens) and mid-call (wall-clock timeout), over-budget = stage fails budgeted, never runaway. SPEC-05 §agent and SPEC-11 need §-amendments (letter-suffix) for the [llm] config schema + compaction contract; selfcheck must PASS.

description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, reproduced twice on the control host. With examples/config.toml (which sets no dashboard.token_file) the daemon boots and serves :7644, but `trouble dashboard token create` mints a tdt_ token that the SAME daemon rejects: GET /incidents -> 401 {"error":{"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002","message":"authentication failed"}} - on a daemon started AFTER the token existed. The token hash in ~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json matches sha256(plaintext) exactly (verified), so mint and store agree; the daemon simply never loaded the file. Mechanism: dashboard.DefaultConfig() TokenFile = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json" (internal/dashboard/config.go:58, a literal tilde); internal/app/dashdeps.go:43 only overrides it when the lifecycle key is non-empty; nothing expands ~ inside the dashboard package, os.Stat fails, and tokens.go readFileIntoSet documents "a missing file yields a valid empty set" - so it fails closed, silently, forever. Blast radius: the dashboard (SPEC-10) is unreachable and the ONLY credential the product can mint is inert, on the documented config path; tests/e2e/cli_smoke.sh passes only because it hands the daemon an absolute token_file. Fix direction: expand ~ (or resolve the path through the same resolver the CLI uses) in DefaultConfig/dashboardConfig, and log a WARN whenever the token store loads as missing/empty so the failure is not silent.

(1) README.md has no install, no run, no config, no first-event recipe: the only commands are `go build ./...` / `go test`; a user who wants to RUN the product must find docs/cmd.md and deploy/README.md themselves. (3) examples/trouble.env documents the dashboard bearer example as `TROUBLE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN=dsh_...` while the CLI mints `tdt_`+43 (docs/cmd.md, cli_smoke.sh:115) - the documented prefix is wrong and the env file is never read as a dashboard credential anyway (token store + IngestionKeys only). (4) docs/cmd.md says the token store keeps only `sha256(token)[:32]`; the store holds 64 hex chars (cli_smoke.sh:121 asserts 64). Fix direction: a 15-line README quickstart (make bin -> minimal config -> absolute token_file -> token create -> curl the on-ramp -> open the dashboard), fix the dsh_/tdt_ and [:32]/[:64] strings, and note that examples/config.toml must be copied AND its zone_windows form is the string form.

title: [P1] Idle-host amplification: 778 records / 74 incidents in 6 minutes from an idle host with 21 distinct sigs - the same sig AND same inKey re-opens a new incident 3-4x (69-142s apart) and one psi sig produced 137 event records
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, measured on a throwaway state root against the live control host (idle, loadavg ~7 but no app activity). Over 6 minutes the daemon wrote 778 ledger records: 684 event, 74 incident, 16 lifecycle, 4 config; ledger grew to 843 KB; /health.json reported events_per_min 204, groups_open 96, incidents_open 74. Only 21 distinct sigs and 21 distinct inKeys exist, yet 74 incident records - i.e. 3-4 incidents per identity: e.g. sig dbus:sha256v1:c158b3e1eac71459 with inKey ink_... at 16:02:10, 16:03:19, 16:05:41 (69s and 142s apart). SPEC/README pin the dedup+merge upsert keyed by sig+inKey with a fold inside the dedup window (AC-22) - same key, same window, new incident. Event level: one psi sig (psi:sha256v1:f8525bc3eea25477) accounts for 137 of 684 event records in 6 min, i.e. the same recurring observation is persisted every sensor cycle. The dbus storm breaker did fire ("rule:dbus_unit_failed: 21 incidents inside 5m0s"), so the breaker works while the fold does not. Projection: ~180k records/day and ~200 MB/day of ledger from ONE idle host, before any real incident; the ledger is append-only, git-distributed and auto-filed, so this growth is permanent. Ask: verify the dedup fold (window values, key derivation, upsert path) and add a per-rule event fold/suppression so a repeating condition is one record with a count, not N records.
acceptance_criteria: a repeated detection with identical sig+inKey inside the dedup window yields ONE incident (test over the real ingest/sensor path)
a repeating rule does not persist one event record per cycle (fold or counter, with the disposition visible)
measure and record records/day + ledger bytes/day on an idle host; compare against an explicit budget
no regression in storm-breaker behaviour (breaker still opens on the configured rate)

title: [P2] Dashboard polish from real use: footer renders an empty version (`trouble v ()`), the budget panel's first server render after boot is blank/zero (fills ~2s later), and the auth-failure throttle 429s a VALID token after prior failures from the same IP
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, all three observed live on a throwaway state root (autonomy=shadow). (1) Every page footer renders `trouble v () - read-mostly dashboard (SPEC-10)` while /health.json reports version c363daf / git_sha c363daf and the budget partial renders "c363daf c363daf" - the footer's version value is empty at render time, so the operator's most visible build stamp is missing while the build is correctly stamped elsewhere. (2) The /incidents page fetched immediately after boot server-renders the budget panel with empty values (`binary`/`rss`/`ledger`/`events` blank, groups open 0, incidents open 0) in the SAME response whose header says "open incidents (74)"; 9 s later /partials/budget carries the real numbers (13.7 MB, 96 groups, 74 incidents). First paint therefore contradicts itself until the first poll lands - and the numbers ARE available (runtime_watermarks in the same /health.json). (3) The auth-failure throttle keys on the client IP, not the credential: after 8-10 failed attempts from one IP (a mistyped/rotated token, or the pre-fix 400s), requests carrying a VALID token get 429 {"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-012","message":"rate limited","detail":"auth_failure_throttle"} with Retry-After: 1 for the whole 60s window. Fix direction: render the version into the footer from the same accessor the health surface uses; seed the first budget render from the same watermark source; and either key the failure throttle on (IP + credential class) or surface a distinct banner so a legitimate operator understands they are throttled, not rejected. (4) heartbeat.json is written with ledger_last_seq=0 and ledger_last_ts="" on every heartbeat - observed across three instances including one whose ledger held 188 records - so the liveness surface a human or an external monitor reads reports a permanently zero sequence while the ledger is advancing (check-stall uses the ledger directly and is unaffected; the field is simply always empty). Fold the same fix as (1): source these values from the accessors that already answer correctly elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: footer shows the version/git_sha the health surface reports

a valid token is not throttled by failures it did not make (or the throttle response is distinguishable from auth rejection)

title: [P1] QA sync ships the whole workdir including gitignored build artifacts: ~/trouble = 141 MB of which 111 MB is .worktrees/ -> phase A took 8.5 min against a documented 60-120s budget

review_notes: Measured on the control host: `du -sh --exclude=.git ~/trouble` = 141M, of which `.worktrees/` = 111M (8 stale worker worktrees, each carrying its own `.git` file), `dagger.db` = 68K, `bin/` (stamped binaries) and `.gitreins/` are shipped too. src: bunker-qa.sh sync_repo() tars with a hardcoded exclude list (.git, node_modules, target, .next, .pnpm-store, .turbo, .cache, dist, build, coverage) and never consults .gitignore. title: [P1] file_findings reports FILED=1 / write_failed:false while the board commit failed: `fatal: pathspec '.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl' is beyond a symbolic link` — the row lands uncommitted
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: Checkpoint output of the file_findings node (run /tmp/dagger-role-qa-1730745-1789670827473332851, project terminal-jail-qa): APPENDED=1 PRIOR=134 TOTAL=135 / FILED=1 / 'fatal: pathspec '.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl' is beyond a symbolic link' with write_failed:false and verdict FINDINGS. Verified on disk: the row exists (~/terminal-jail/.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl contains QA-TERMINAL-JAIL-QA-1, 135 rows) and `git -C ~/terminal-jail status --porcelain` shows ` M .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl` = UNCOMMITTED. title: [P1] The QA lane grades and closes a run CLEAN one minute into a 7-15 minute battery: single collect attempt, filed:0, real cells never pulled, agent left to TTL
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: Observed end to end on the targeted tick: `launch` cell written 22:10:15Z (battery started detached, toolchain-bootstrap OK / fresh-install in progress on the agent at 22:10:45Z), then `parse_cells` ran its ONE PHASE-B collect attempt at ~22:11Z, got RUNNING (early-exit, no destroy), and the pipeline went straight to `interpret` (22:11:13) and `file_findings` (22:11:19) -> verdict CLEAN, findings [], filed 0, summary 'phase-B collect has not reported results, so no findings are derivable'. The battery was ~1 minute into a 7-15 minute run; its later cells (ci-pass, chaos-*) were never collected, no ledger row records them, and the agent is left to its 4h TTL. This is the premature-completion pattern the QA lane exists to catch, implemented in the lane itself: the verdict is honest about having no evidence, but the RUN still terminates as CLEAN, so a failing CI/chaos cell produces no row, no gap, no retry. Design quotes (hermes-dagger examples/coding-hermes/qa.ts ~L150-190): 'PHASE A: LAUNCH, never wait ... Phase B (collect) runs at the top of parse_cells and pulls the cells once it has finished; if nothing collects it, the agent's TTL (default 4h) reclaims it.' Fix direction: poll collect to completion (bounded, e.g. until ~20 min) before interpreting, or emit an explicit UNVERIFIED/deferred row + a scheduled second pass so the finished cells reach the board; never let a still-running battery end as CLEAN.

title: [P1] Clean-machine native suite is RED: TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange fails on a fresh bunker box but passes on the control host (mtime-fingerprint assertion is filesystem/host fragile)
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 — cell recovered by collecting the battery the QA lane closed CLEAN before it finished (QA-LANE-6)
review_notes: Battery on agent-host-2 (agent ed361cdd, tree synced from HEAD 28c3c01, go 1.26.5 bootstrapped): ci-pass FAIL 'native rc=1: FAIL github.com/totalwindupflightsystems/trouble/internal/sensors 74.846s ...' with the failing test verbatim: '--- FAIL: TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange (0.00s) | reload_test.go:310: the mtime fingerprint did not change after an edit'. Control host, same commit: `go test ./internal/sensors/ -run TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange -count=1` -> ok 0.006s at load_avg 3.08, i.e. PASS. So this is clean-machine/environment-specific, not a deterministic break: the assertion compares mtimes after an edit, which depends on the filesystem's mtime granularity and on the tar-synced tree's timestamps on the agent (the battery ships the tree via tar + `git init && add -A && commit`, so file times are rewritten). Same env-fragility family as QA-TROUBLE-1 (RSS budget) and QA-TROUBLE-2 (scrub wall-clock budget). Fix direction: make the fingerprint check granularity-independent (compare content hashes or force mtime with explicit values after a sleep >granularity), and note it in the reload contract; then re-run the clean-machine cell to confirm green. NOTE: the lane never filed this — it graded the run CLEAN ~1 minute into a 13.9-minute battery and moved on.

title: [P1] internal/sensors TestResolveManagers red on any host whose uid != 1000: dbus_test.go fixture hardcodes user:1000 so the self-vs-uid dedup never collapses (len 3, want 2)
reasoning: QA foreman cycle 2026-09-18 — fresh-system CI pass + chaos on agent-host-2 (agent 681b9e63, ci-pass cell)
review_notes: REPRODUCED on the clean QA agent in all three legs that run the suite (ci-pass act leg ci.log, ci-pass native leg native.log, chaos-resource 3G-cap leg res.log), identical line: internal/sensors TestResolveManagers — dbus_test.go:99 "managers = [system user:1018 user:1000], want system + one deduped uid". ROOT CAUSE read from source, not inferred: resolveManagers() (internal/sensors/dbus.go:478-510) dedupes correctly by uid (seen[uid] map), but the test fixture sets sensors.dbus.user_managers = ["self","user:1000","uid:1000","bogus"] and asserts len(got)==2 — which only holds when the TEST PROCESS uid is 1000, so "self" collides with user:1000/uid:1000 and the three real entries collapse to one. On the bunker agent (uid 1018) and under act (root = uid 0) "self" resolves to a DIFFERENT uid, two distinct uids survive dedup, len(got)==3, deterministic FAIL. The product code is correct; the assertion hardcodes the runner's uid, so `go test ./...` is red on every clean machine whose uid is not 1000 (any container running as root or a service user). REPRO (any non-1000 host): cd ~/trouble && go test ./internal/sensors/ -run TestResolveManagers -count=1 → "managers = [system user:<selfuid> user:1000], want system + one deduped uid". FIX SHAPE: build the fixture from os.Getuid() (fmt.Sprintf("user:%d", os.Getuid())) or use ["self","uid:<self>","bogus"] so the dedup path is exercised on every host. DEDUPE: distinct defect from the open rows on this board — TRBL-004 and QA-TROUBLE-1/2 cover the load-sensitive wall-clock/RSS budget family (TestAmortizedThroughput, TestDeriveNeverBlocks, TestRSSContributionIsBounded, TestScrubBudget); this failure is uid-dependent and load-independent (it also failed in the 3G-cap leg where sentinel/research/skills were green). Ambiguity stated honestly: it would pass on a single-user box running as uid 1000.
